solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Against orders being given to achieve results

parts.note: con is the opposite of pro, as in pros and cons
orders and sequences are both arrangements in a set succession

explanation.surface: Defying instructions is supposedly the way to get things done.
explanation.definitionFit: Consequences are the outcomes or effects that follow from an action, which is what results are.

clue.text: The ranks irate, needing inner energy? One should provide fruit

parts.note: OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

indicators.note: the abbreviation must go into the middle of the word just given

parts.note: irate means angry
E is the abbreviation for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Angry soldiers need a boost of energy, perhaps from fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: An orangery is a glasshouse for growing orange trees, so a building that supplies fruit.

clue.text: Group of players sounded disappointed in broadcast

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard rather than read, so the sound of the word counts

parts.note: to sigh is to make a sound of disappointment

explanation.surface: Fans made a disappointed noise during the coverage of the team.
explanation.definitionFit: A side is a team, a group of players in a match.

clue.text: After pursuit I had one held to be examined

indicators.note: the second piece comes after the word for pursuit

parts.note: a quest is a pursuit or search

indicators.note: one is held inside the contraction

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I had
taken as written

explanation.surface: After a chase, someone held a person to be questioned.
explanation.definitionFit: To be questioned is to be interrogated, so examined by questioning.

clue.text: Nurse getting out drug? There must be safeguard

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters of nurse are rearranged

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A nurse dispensing drugs must have safeguards in place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges NURSE to make ENSUR, then E is added.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensure something is to make it certain or secure it, so to safeguard it.

clue.text: Buddies offering prayers, holding on

indicators.note: the word for prayers holds the small word inside

parts.note: cries are pleas or entreaties, prayers offered up
taken as written

explanation.surface: Friends are praying, carrying on.
explanation.definitionFit: Cronies are close companions or pals, so buddies.

clue.text: She sipped her sloppy food

indicators.note: sloppy means messy and careless, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A woman slurped her messy dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: SHE stays in place at the front; 'sloppy' rearranges SIPPEDHER to make PHERDSPIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Shepherd's pie is minced lamb topped with mashed potato, a British dish and so an example of food.

clue.text: Complete act as substitute

definitions.meaning: to complete a form by writing in the details
to stand in for someone temporarily

explanation.definitionFit: To fill in means both to complete a form and to deputise for someone absent.

clue.text: Capital city a short distance to the west

indicators.note: in an across clue westward is leftward, so the letters are read from right to left

parts.note: a mil is a thousandth of an inch, or short for millimetre, a tiny distance

explanation.surface: A capital lies just a little way off to the west.
explanation.definitionFit: Lima is the capital of Peru, so it is an example of a capital city.

clue.text: Set of rules which may mean men are 'tied'?

definitions.text: Set of rules which may mean men are 'tied'?

parts.words: Set of rules which may mean men are 'tied'?
parts.note: the quoted word pretends to mean bound or drawn level, but it means wearing a necktie, as a formal dress requirement for an event might insist

explanation.surface: Some regulation apparently leaves the men in a tie or tied up.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal attire requirement is a set of rules about clothing, often demanding that men wear ties.

clue.text: Start to attack and exceed the bounds of reason?

definitions.meaning: soldiers in First World War trenches climbed over the parapet to begin an assault

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase originally meant leaving the trench to attack, and idiomatically means going too far.

clue.text: Compel old boy to be deceitful? There's little good in that

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

indicators.note: the small piece is placed inside the word just given, the word 'that' pointing back to it

parts.note: to lie is to be deceitful
G is the short form, a little version, of good

explanation.surface: A former pupil is forced into deceit, with hardly any good in it.
explanation.definitionFit: To oblige someone can mean to compel or constrain them by force of law or circumstance.

clue.text: Sea creature has first to swim

indicators.note: swimming letters move about freely, so the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A marine animal gets to swim first.
explanation.definitionFit: A starfish is a star-shaped echinoderm living on the seabed, an example of a marine animal.

clue.text: Time in training device may be encouraging man

indicators.note: the letter goes inside the word for the training machine

parts.note: a simulator is a machine used to train pilots and drivers

explanation.surface: Time spent in a flight trainer may spur a man on.
explanation.definitionFit: A stimulator is something or someone that encourages activity, so an encouraging agent.

clue.text: Worship may be helping, even when strange at first

indicators.note: the rearranged piece comes at the start, ahead of the next one
strange letters are oddly arranged, so the word even is rearranged

parts.note: a ration is an allotted helping of food

explanation.surface: Devotion might be just a portion of food, and an odd one at that.
explanation.walkthrough: 'helping' looks like an act of assistance, but it is a portion of food; 'strange' rearranges EVEN to make VENE.
explanation.definitionFit: Veneration is deep reverence or adoration, a synonym of worship as a noun.

clue.text: Prime requirements for the student are rubber and ruler

indicators.note: the prime, or first, letters are what is taken from the next four words

explanation.surface: Essentials for a pupil are an eraser and a measuring stick.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's 'ruler' is a measuring stick; as the definition it is a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsar was the emperor of Russia, so a type of ruler or sovereign.

clue.text: Faller noted before start of Cup Final

definitions.text: Faller noted before start of Cup Final

parts.words: Faller noted before start of Cup Final
parts.note: noted means set to music and sung: the hymn Abide with Me, sung before the FA Cup Final kick-off, begins with something that falls fast

explanation.surface: A player who fell was spotted just before the final kicked off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Faller' tempts solvers toward Eve; it is the evening hour that falls fast in the first line of the hymn. The FA Cup Final is English football's showpiece match at Wembley.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventide is a poetic word for evening, the close of the day.

clue.text: Stranded presumably and not feeling very well

definitions.meaning: like rope, made of twisted strands
informal British for poorly or under the weather

explanation.definitionFit: Ropy means rope-like and fibrous, and colloquially in Britain it means slightly unwell or of poor quality.

clue.text: Opening with image cut below it — an architectural feature

parts.note: a port is an opening, as a porthole or a computer port

indicators.note: cut means the last letter is chopped off

parts.note: an icon is a religious image

explanation.surface: A doorway shows a cropped picture beneath it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'below it' places the trimmed image under the opening, which in a down clue means after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A portico is a porch of columns at a building's entrance, a feature of classical design.

clue.text: Resistant and high-handed, very contained

indicators.note: the abbreviation sits held inside the longer word

parts.note: imperious means arrogantly domineering, high-handed

explanation.surface: Someone is tough and arrogant, though very restrained.
explanation.definitionFit: Impervious means not allowing anything through or not affected, so resistant.

clue.text: Vision's funny, beginning to go

indicators.note: the first letter is removed

parts.note: jocular means joking or humorous

explanation.surface: Someone's eyesight is behaving oddly, starting to fail.
explanation.definitionFit: Ocular means relating to the eye, so of vision, matching the possessive adjective.

clue.text: Going mad circling bottom of oak tree

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the next piece
mad letters are crazily mixed up
in a down clue the bottom is the last letter

explanation.surface: Someone goes crazy walking round the foot of an oak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mad' rearranges GOING to make GINGO, which goes round K.
explanation.definitionFit: The ginkgo is the maidenhair tree, an ancient Chinese species and so an example of a tree.

clue.text: One bishop after another in tricky situation — ghastly!

indicators.note: the bishops are placed inside the word for a tricky situation

parts.note: to be in a hole is to be in a tricky situation

indicators.note: the first two pieces come after the title abbreviation

parts.note: another bishop, here RR, the abbreviation for Right Reverend, a bishop's title
I is the Roman numeral for one
B is the chess notation for a bishop

explanation.surface: Bishop follows bishop into a dreadful predicament, which is awful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One bishop after another' reads as a stream of clergy, but it is I and B placed after a second bishop given by his title Right Reverend.
explanation.definitionFit: Horrible and ghastly are synonyms, both meaning shockingly unpleasant.

clue.text: Doughnuts to get rid of before lunchtime?

indicators.note: the cancelling word comes ahead of the time

parts.note: to annul something is to cancel or get rid of it
lunch is traditionally at one o'clock, and I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Doughnuts need to be cleared away before lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: Lunchtime is taken as one o'clock, giving the Roman numeral I.
explanation.definitionFit: Annuli are ring-shaped figures, and doughnuts are ring-shaped, so they are examples.

clue.text: Stay for theatrical item

definitions.meaning: a support that holds something up
an object used by actors on stage

explanation.definitionFit: A prop is both a support or buttress and, short for property, an object used on stage.

clue.text: Fraud with phoney tickets right outside front of racetrack

indicators.note: the letters go round the following piece
phoney means fake, so the letters are rearranged
the front letter is taken

explanation.surface: A con man selling forged race tickets right outside the track entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'phoney' rearranges TICKETS to make TICKSTE; with R added this goes 'outside' the R from 'front of racetrack', which sits after the T.
explanation.definitionFit: A trickster is a cheat who deceives people, so a fraud.

clue.text: One managed to establish a republic

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
ran, as in ran a business, means managed

explanation.surface: Someone was in charge of setting up a republic.
explanation.definitionFit: Iran is the Islamic Republic of Iran, so an example of a republic.

clue.text: See sort of artist in garret hop-hop around

indicators.note: around signals the letters are moved round into a new order

explanation.surface: Look at an artist dancing around their attic.
explanation.definitionFit: A photographer is a person who makes art with a camera, a kind of artist.
